nodes.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve idempotence for terminal close calls**

After a stream has reached `Closed`, calling `close(context:)` with an already-cancelled or expired context throws here before `beginClose` can observe the terminal state. A repeated close therefore fails instead of being a no-op, unlike the no-argument overload and the other resource implementations; check for a terminal lifecycle before applying the context preflight while retaining the preflight for streams that still need closing.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L63-L64](https://github.com/lIlIIlIll/Wirestack/blob/86bd99f3a97d343302c212d1dddbca05f5f14ee3/AGENTS.md#L63-L64)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Make abort interrupt an in-flight graceful close**

When graceful close has entered the production delegate but `socket.close()` has not returned, `StdNetTransport.close` has already set `closed` and claimed `nativeClosed` (`src/internal/transport_stdnet/package.cj:327-337`). A concurrent call here publishes `Aborted`, but `delegate.abort()` then sees `closed` and does nothing, so it neither applies abortive close nor interrupts the outstanding graceful close, and eventual graceful completion is mislabeled as an abort; publish `Aborted` only when the delegate actually claims abort ownership, or allow the delegate to upgrade an in-flight close.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L61-L64](https://github.com/lIlIIlIll/Wirestack/blob/86bd99f3a97d343302c212d1dddbca05f5f14ee3/AGENTS.md#L61-L64)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

decision: Preserve the first native close owner. Terminal repeated close is a no-op before context callbacks; an abort request cannot relabel a graceful native owner.

native_probe.method_rename_note: Only the private SPI observer name changes between probe variants; the scenario and assertions are identical.
native_probe.scope: A real native graceful close produces peer EOF, then a gate holds the wrapper close return while a concurrent abort calls the real native delegate. A second case repeats real terminal close with stopped contexts.
native_probe.limitation: The gate is after native close returns, not inside a blocked SDK socket.close. This proves real delegate ownership and wrapper labeling; no native close interruption or upgrade is claimed.
